time.desc: The university involved publicly clarified the rumors related to the party’s postgraduate admissions, denying that it had ever released or revoked its list of candidates for doctoral admissions, which triggered deletions by many reprinters.

The version of the civil judgment circulated on the Internet was suspected of deleting key paragraphs and evidence records, triggering intensive verification and controversy over "the judgment was tampered with/disseminated out of context."
The party appealed against the first-instance judgment and was formally accepted by the intermediate court, and the case entered the second-instance procedure.

The graduate thesis of the university involved was removed from the public academic platform, and the platform customer service disclosed that retraction materials need to be submitted through the process between the author and the school.
The court issued a second-instance judgment on the sexual harassment liability dispute, rejected the appeal and upheld the first-instance result, and the civil dispute reached a final conclusion.

The university involved issued a disposition notice: revoking the sanctions against the accused students and imposing sanctions on the relevant management and tutor responsibilities. It also determined that the degree thesis involved was only a large number of irregularities and did not constitute principled academic misconduct. The degree was maintained.
The parties concerned publicly confronted others and defended themselves through social accounts, triggering a new round of public opinion fluctuations.

The person concerned claimed on social platforms that he had passed the public service examination and then quickly changed his story and denied it. This was widely questioned as a false information act to create a topic and triggered centralized supervision.
Blogger exposed the accuser's falsification of test transcripts and academic integrity issues in past award-winning papers
Platform posts allege that there are organized accounts that continue to clear ground for the accuser and discredit the accused, implying manipulation of public opinion.
Mainstream media published comments criticizing the universities involved for using excuses to wait for superiors and refusing to promptly correct and punish them.
A blogger's article supporting the accuser was blocked and removed from the platform a few hours after it was published. The blogger said he was besieged by organized reports.

The school has not announced the results of the review for more than 20 days and is accused of hiding the disciplinary documents on the school network, which is only visible within the school. This is interpreted as waiting to see the final judicial review.
Several high school classmates and alumni of the accused party provided real-name materials to reporters to prove their history of misconduct in high school.
Media reported that a large number of brotherly aid accounts have emerged on social platforms to teach men strategies for dealing with sexual harassment accusations and even violent confrontations.
The main person in charge of the party committee of the university involved was replaced. The day after the new person in charge took office, the school worked overtime to issue a correction notice.

The announcements from the universities involved showed that each of them had fifty major objections, triggering further public doubts about the zero cost of false accusations and the attribution of responsibility.
Another university (Institution B) officially revoked Person B’s doctoral admission qualification and removed him from the list of proposed doctoral students.
Person C, a third party, formally filed a lawsuit against Institution K, demanding a public apology from the school.
After losing the first instance, Character B was accused of continuing to incite online violence and threatening and harassing the judge presiding over the case.
In addition to Character B’s dissertation being removed from the shelves, his mentor’s related articles have also been withdrawn.
Organization K clarified in the report that the rumor that "Character B's uncle holds the title A in the school" is not true

Institution K issued a more detailed review description, saying that an investigation team composed of five experts investigated 21 people and reviewed 91 pieces of evidence. It determined that Person B’s dissertation was not plagiarized and the degree would not be revoked.
